task: Task 1: AS Chemistry 3.1.1 mass spectrometry concept and answer-level review

reviewedAreas: Time of flight stages and comparisons
reviewScope.limits: Selected content review against 3.1.1: not a full independent examiner-approval of 88 answers or the whole Chemistry mock syllabus.

findings.finding: Historical front refers to four steps by grouping detection/data analysis; AQA names ionisation, acceleration, drift, detection and data analysis as five stages.
findings.fix: Ask for five ordered stages, preserving original ID and progress.
findings.newBack: Ionisation → acceleration → ion drift → ion detection → data analysis.

findings.finding: At fixed kinetic energy, the simple flight-time mass comparison must specify equivalent charge to avoid a misleading inference about the mass-to-charge ratio.
findings.fix: Require equal charge and kinetic energy and ask about the mass-dependent speed.
findings.newBack: Lighter ions move faster and arrive at the detector sooner.

findings.finding: Lower m/z is not generally equivalent to lower mass for ions of unequal charge when their kinetic energies are forced equal.
findings.fix: Specify singly charged ions with equal kinetic energy before comparing m/z.
findings.newBack: Lower m/z, because the lighter ion moves faster.

newMockCards.why: Direct recall of what ionises a neutral gaseous sample by electron impact, rather than only the resulting positive-ion formula.
Direct recall of the measured ion arrival time, distinguished from derived mass-to-charge ratio and peak abundance.

remainingWork: Review AS Chemistry original cards by specification subsection and correct genuine errors.
Audit exam-answer markers for method credit and equivalents.
